bullets: Cheap readers get far, not far enough. On 300 scans, local OCR + rules reads date and total right 73% of the time at $0, a local 3B vision model 83% (28 s on a 4 GB laptop GPU), Flash-Lite 97% at $0.54 per 1,000, 3.6 Flash 98% at $1.42. On 200 phone photos: local OCR 55%, local VLM 81%, cloud 87%.

Routing is cheap; the escalation signal is the bottleneck. An oracle sends 27% of receipts to the cloud for 98.7% at $0.15 per 1,000. The rule router (two readers agree, confidence ≥ 0.9) sends 56% for 95.7%; code checks lift accepted answers to 96.9% at a 4% review load. A logistic model on 13 tier-1 signals (AUC 0.89, out of fold) did not beat the rule on scans and gained 0.5 points on photos: the gap needs richer signals, not a bigger model.

Code catches what the model cannot see about itself. With no answer key, the checks caught 38 of the local model's 51 wrong answers and 5 of Flash-Lite's 8. Of the 18 that slipped through on scans, 16 were a different printed amount (cash tendered, a subtotal), not a misread. On 43 adversarial receipts all three models ignored all 16 injections, every date and arithmetic trap tripped a gate, nothing leaked.
